(1) Write a function called `mean_ci()` that takes the arguments listed below and returns either a confidence interval for a single mean or a confidence interval for the difference in means (per user specification). Also allow the user to specify either a 90%, 95% or 99% confidence interval. 

* `x` (no default value)
* `y` (default value is `NULL` which corresponds to `one.mean` option for the `type` argument)
* `type` (default value is `one.mean`, other value is `two.means`)
* `naFlag` or `...` (to allow the user a way to tell the function how to handle missing values)
* `conf.level` (default value is 0.95, other allowed values are 0.90 and 0.99; allows the user to specify a confidence level)

Include a a way to check whether the vectors of `x` and `y` are numeric and thus such a confidence interval is appropriate. Also be sure to check the `conf.level` argument and return a useful error if the user does not specify one of the allowed levels. Be sure to give informative error messages for any mis-use of the function. Code will be provided to help you error check your function.

```{r}
#Put your code to read in the data here

```

If you would like a way to check that your confidence intervals are correct, here is the code I will use to check that your function works appropriately:
```{r echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
set.seed(8675309)
x <- rnorm(50)
y <- rnorm(30)

mean_ci(x)   # should get [1] -0.1404677  0.3458514
mean_ci(x, conf.level = 0.9)   # should get [1] -0.09791482  0.30329849

mean_ci(x, y, type="two.means")   # should get [1] -0.1875458  0.7320355

# checking the na.rm piece
x2 <- c(x, NA)
y2 <- c(y, NA)
mean_ci(x2, y2, type="two.means", naFlag = FALSE)  # should get [1] NA NA
mean_ci(x2, y2, type="two.means")   # should get [1] -0.1875458  0.7320355

# checking the numeric piece
x3 <- c("hi", "how", "are", "you", "?")
mean_ci(x3) # should return informative error message
mean_ci(x3, y2, type = "two.means") # should return informative error message

# check the type piece
mean_ci(x2, y2, type = "two.groups") # should return informative error message

# check the conf level
mean_ci(x2, y2, type = "two.means", conf.level = 0.8) # should return informative error message
```


(2) Write a function called `prop_ci()` that takes the arguments listed below and returns either a confidence interval for a single proportion or a confidence interval for the difference in proportions depending on those arguments. Also allow the user to specify either a 90%, 95% or 99% confidence interval.  

* `x` (no default value, but must be a vector containing 0, 1 and `NA` only)
* `y` (default value is `NULL` which corresponds to `one.mean` option for the `type` argument; must also contain only 0, 1 and `NA` values)
* `type` (default value is `one.prop`, other value is `two.props`)
* `naFlag` or `...` (to allow the user a way to tell the function how to handle missing values)
* `conf.level` (default value is 0.95, other allowed values are 0.90 and 0.99; allows the user to specify a confidence level)

Include a way to check whether the vectors of `x` and `y` are 0/1 vectors and thus such a confidence interval is appropriate. Also be sure to check the `conf.level` argument and return a useful error if the user does not specify one of the allowed levels. Be sure to give informative error messages for any mis-use of the function. Code will be provided to help you error check your function.

```{r}
#Put your code for this here

```


If you would like a way to check that your confidence intervals are correct, here is the code I will use to check that your function works appropriately:
```{r echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
set.seed(8675309)
x <- rbinom(50, 1, .5)
y <- rbinom(30, 1, .2)

prop_ci(x)   # should get [1] 0.4196006 0.7003994
prop_ci(x, conf.level = 0.9)   # should get [1] 0.4441705 0.6758295

prop_ci(x, y, type="two.props")   # should get [1] 0.1978071 0.5888596
prop_ci(x, y, type="two.props", conf.level = 0.99)   # should get [1] 0.1391492 0.6475175

# checking the na.rm piece
x2 <- c(x, NA)
y2 <- c(y, NA)
prop_ci(x2, y2, type="two.props", naFlag = FALSE)  # should get [1] NA NA or an error message depending on how checked for binary vectors
prop_ci(x2, y2, type="two.props")   # should get [1] 0.1978071 0.5888596

# checking the binary piece
x3 <- c(3,4,5,2,0,1)
prop_ci(x3)
prop_ci(x3, y2, type = "two.props")

# check the type piece
prop_ci(x2, y2, type = "two.groups")

# check the conf.level piece
prop_ci(x2, y2, conf.level = 0.8)
```

ratio_ci(n1 = 20, n2 = 10, p1 = .5, p2 = .7)   # should get [1] 0.08275144 2.21958041
ratio_ci(n1 = 20, n2 = 10, p1 = .5, p2 = .7, type = "odds.ratio")   # should get [1] 0.08275144 2.21958041
